title: Shishir Jain v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. & Another
coram: Krishna Murari & Ravindra Nath Kakkar, JJ.
disposition: Writ petition allowed; impugned 'final notice' letters quashed, licensee left free to make a proper final assessment
headnote: The condition precedent to a provisional assessment under Section 126(1) of the Electricity Act, 2003 is the assessing officer's recorded conclusion, based on inspection, that the person is indulging in unauthorised use of electricity — such satisfaction cannot rest on mere vagaries without a fair opportunity of hearing. Clause 8.1(b) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 mandates, after a consumer files objections to a provisional assessment/show-cause notice, a personal hearing before any final assessment is made. A licensee cannot, after a consumer has filed timely objections to a provisional assessment (following a prior court order permitting such objections), simply issue a 'final notice' demanding payment of the same provisionally-assessed amount — without any notice of hearing, without considering the objections, and without passing or serving any actual final assessment order — and treat that notice as enforceable; such notices, issued to pressure the consumer into payment while dehors the statutory Section 126/Clause 8.1 procedure, are liable to be quashed, without prejudice to the licensee thereafter conducting a proper final assessment in accordance with law.

holding_units.code: Electricity Act, 2003 (s.126(1)/(3)) read with U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 (Clause 8.1(a)/(b))
holding_units.clause: 8.1(b)(iii) (personal hearing after objections to provisional assessment, before final assessment)
holding_units.topic: A 'final notice' demanding payment of a provisionally assessed amount, issued without any hearing on the consumer's timely-filed objections and without an actual reasoned final assessment order, is dehors the Section 126/Clause 8.1 procedure and must be quashed
holding_units.question: Can a licensee enforce payment of a provisionally assessed theft-related amount by issuing a 'final notice' after the consumer has filed objections, without giving any notice of personal hearing, considering the objections, or passing/serving a reasoned final assessment order?
holding_units.holding: No. Section 126(1)'s provisional assessment requires the assessing officer's recorded conclusion of unauthorised use, which itself cannot be reached without a fair opportunity of hearing given the potential overlap with s.135 investigation. Clause 8.1(b)(iii) of the Supply Code specifically requires a personal hearing after the consumer files objections to the provisional assessment/show-cause notice, before any final order is passed. Here, after the petitioner filed timely objections (pursuant to an earlier court order permitting him to do so and deposit 50% of the provisional amount for restoration), the licensee neither gave notice of hearing nor considered the objections, yet issued 'final notice' letters (4.3.2017, repeated 17.3.2017) simply reiterating the original provisional-assessment figure as though finally established, without ever serving any actual reasoned final assessment order. This is dehors the statutory procedure (following Ashok Kumar, Kamil, and Hazi Mohd. Yaseen) — a consumer cannot be compelled to pay a provisional-assessment amount as if final, absent a proper final assessment after hearing. The two impugned notices were quashed, with liberty to the licensee to conduct the final assessment properly, in accordance with the Act and the Code.
holding_units.limiting_facts: The petitioner's LMV-1 (residential) connection was subjected to a s.135(1)(e) FIR and provisional assessment (Rs. 1,74,725) after an inspection alleged the premises was being run as a commercial girls'/boys' hostel (attracting LMV-2 commercial tariff); a prior writ petition secured restoration on 50% deposit and leave to object; objections were duly filed, but the licensee then issued 'final notice' letters demanding the full amount without any hearing or reasoned final order.

principle_tags.application: After a consumer files objections to a theft-related provisional assessment, Clause 8.1(b)(iii) requires an actual personal hearing before any final assessment can be made; a bare 'final notice' reiterating the provisional figure, without a hearing or reasoned order, is unenforceable — reinforcing the corpus's cluster of s.126/Clause 8.1 procedural-strictness rulings (SCJ-069, SCJ-087, SCJ-092, SCJ-111).
